references.text: God forbids exploiting widows and orphans: "You shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child" ([ref:Exod 22:22|Exodus 22:22]). The scribes who "devour widows' houses" break this fundamental command.

Isaiah pronounces woe on those who enact unjust laws and deprive the weak of their rights, to plunder widows and make orphans their prey ([ref:Isa 10:1-2|Isaiah 10:1-2]). The same kind of exploitation that Jesus accuses the scribes of.

Ezekiel condemns prophets and leaders who are like roaring lions devouring people and taking valuables: "they devour people, take goods and treasures" ([ref:Ezek 22:25|Ezekiel 22:25]). A parallel to the scribes who devour widows' houses.

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers" ([ref:Matt 23:14|Matthew 23:14]). The same accusation in a longer pronouncement of woe.

Mark's parallel passage: "They devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers. They will receive the greater condemnation" ([ref:Mark 12:40|Mark 12:40]). Almost word-for-word parallel to Luke 20:47.

Jesus warns of the stricter judgment awaiting hypocrites: "You serpents, you brood of vipers! How are you to escape being sentenced to hell?" ([ref:Matt 23:33|Matthew 23:33]). Related to "they will receive the greater condemnation" (περισσότερον κρίμα).
James warns that teachers will be judged more strictly ([ref:Jas 3:1|James 3:1]). The same principle as in Luke 20:47 – those who hold a leadership position and abuse it will be judged more severely.

Micah condemns those who plan evil and seize others' fields and houses by force ([ref:Mic 2:1-2|Micah 2:1-2]). A parallel to the accusation of "devouring widows' houses" – taking property from the defenseless.

Jesus warns against those who pray to be seen by people, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on street corners ([ref:Matt 6:5|Matthew 6:5]). Related to the accusation of making long prayers for a pretense (προφάσει μακρὰ προσεύχονται).

God rejects the people's prayers because they do not practice justice, and instead calls them to help the oppressed, the fatherless, and widows ([ref:Isa 1:15-17|Isaiah 1:15-17]). The contrast between empty prayer and genuine care for widows reflects the accusation in Luke 20:47.
